title: feat(plugin-audit): sys_comment gains a writer-stamped object_name + record_id pair with a backfill, and the comment-thread read gate leafs over it (ADR-0139 E7)
body:
Fixes #23857
Clause-②: yes

ADR-0139 E7, comments half, by the ruling on #23732 (record `6212058353`, batch #354 item 2: letter A on Q1, A on Q2, maintainer 「同意」). `sys_comment` gains a writer-stamped parent pair, and the comment-thread read gate narrows by it with one `ReadableIds` leaf per parent object, with no pre-scan. #23732 remains open; the seat handles it as the ruling's item 6 says.

## Rollout (the changeset's first paragraph)

**Run `os migrate comment-parent-pair --apply` at once after upgrading.** Until it runs, the comments written before the upgrade carry no pair, and the gate answers them by the bounded thread probe it always had: at most 2,000 candidate rows per read, fail closed. So a broad comment list (one not scoped to a single record's thread) can omit comments the reader may see, and its `total` agrees with the short list. A record's own thread is unaffected. The door copies `os migrate activity-changed-fields` (E6, PR #23814) one for one: `--database-url`, `--apply`, `--yes`, `--force`, `--json`; dry run by default; idempotent. Same measured difference as E6: the columns arrive with the upgraded deployment's schema sync, which `--apply` performs itself, so a dry run against a database no upgraded process has opened cannot read them and exits 1.

## What changed

- **The pair** (`objects/sys-comment.object.ts`). `object_name` and `record_id` are `Field.text`, `readonly`, not required, and indexed together as `(object_name, record_id)`. `thread_id` stays the authored key. There is no ADR-0087 conversion and no writer change.
- **One planner**, `planCommentParentPair` (`comment-access-hooks.ts`). It parses the thread with `parseCommentThreadId`, the parse every comment gate authorizes by. A thread that names no record gets `null` / `null`.
- **Who can write the pair:**
  - Create: a `beforeInsert` hook stamps every row, for every caller, the system included, and overwrites any value the writer sent. The engine's create-side readonly strip skips `sys_` objects, so this hook is the guard, as it is for `is_edited`.
  - The re-point rule: an update that names `thread_id` is re-stamped from it.
  - An update that names either column without a thread: the update stamp re-derives the pair from the row's stored thread, for every caller, and drops it when there is no stored row. It does not rely on the engine's strip, which under `preserveAudit` (the REST import's `treatAsHistorical`) keeps a readonly value. A multi-row update of this kind over rows whose threads name different records is refused whole by the stamp itself, not by the engine's key-set divergence check (`VALIDATION_ERROR` / 400, nothing written), because one `SET` clause cannot carry two pairs. Over rows sharing one thread, it stores that thread's pair. Pinned on a real engine and through the REST import (patch rounds 1–2, addenda `6216192076` and `6217048956`).
  - The backfill's SYSTEM by-id update: the stamp re-derives its pair from the thread the row holds at write time. That narrows the backfill's race to the one engine call; it does not close it.
  - Both hooks stamp only when the registered `sys_comment` declares the pair. This is E6's `declaresActivityStampColumns` precedent, for harnesses that register their own `sys_comment`.
- **The gate** (`installCommentReadVisibility`). It is now `computeParentRecordFilter` from `parent-record-read-gate.ts`. That function is imported, not edited, so no third copy of the D5 classification is written. It runs over the comment's pair with a `commentThreadGate()` config:
  - The parent set is every registered object except `sys_comment`. All of `AUDIT_EXCLUDED_OBJECTS` is named, because a comment can hang off any record. This is the same set `parseCommentThreadId` accepts.
  - D5's three classes are routed to the bounded probe by name and up front, never by catching a refusal. So are the two whole-read states: no `canReadObject` (no leaf is written without it) and an engine that cannot classify.
  - Rows with no stamped pair get one more branch, ORed in: the old bounded thread probe, restricted to `object_name IS NULL`. Its branch carries that conjunct, so it never selects a stamped row. Rows the backfill has not reached are probed, never leafed.
  - A `sys_comment` that declares no pair keeps the thread probe over every row, and the gate says so once.
  - `next()` sits outside the gate's `try`, so a composition refusal (on `driver-mongodb`, a 500) is the read's own failure (D3).
  - `AuditPlugin` passes the security source.
- **Reactions are unchanged** (Q2, D5.2). They are recorded on #23857 with the reading member 1,763 of 2,300 and administrator `total` 2,000 of 2,601.
- **The backfill**, `backfillCommentParentPair` (`comment-parent-pair-backfill.ts`, exported from `src/index.ts`):
  - It works in E6's shape: a SYSTEM keyset walk on `object_name $null`, then a single-id SYSTEM update of both columns.
  - It updates under `preserveAudit` with the row's stored `updated_at`, so no comment's `updated_at` moves. Measured through the door.
  - A thread that names no record is counted as `unparented` and left unstamped.
  - A refused page read is counted, so the door exits 1.
- **The door** `os migrate comment-parent-pair`, registered in the one-shot family table, the JSON-purity family and the absent-database roster.
- **Docs and generated files:**
  - `deployment/cli.mdx`: a section and a table row.
  - `platform-checklist/areas/cli.json`: 17 → 18 subcommands.
  - The plugin-audit i18n bundles, regenerated and translated.
  - The tenant-audit census, regenerated: 226 → 227 write sites, from the backfill's update. The hand-written prose figures follow.
  - The checklist item `attachments-storage.read-inherits-parent-rls`, revision 5, carries the two notes from `6206614195`.

Landing places: everything is in `plugin-audit`, the CLI door and its three family registrations, dogfood, docs, and the generated files the gates regenerate. None of `writeAudit`, `packages/spec`, `objectql`, `core`, any driver, `parent-record-read-gate.ts`, `migrate/organization-ownership*`, `apply.ts`, `docs/adr/**` or objectui is touched.

## Evidence

Local readings at head `e499adaf6` (with `origin/main` `34b740f2d` merged in), on the shared box, under `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`. Patch rounds 1–2 (to `7d41db652`) change only the update stamp, docblocks, the changeset and tests. The read gate is untouched. The dev re-read these numbers at `7d41db652` (supplement `6217097662`), and they are unchanged: real engine member 2,303 of 2,303 and administrator `total` 2,605 of 2,605; the stack served 2,050 of 2,050. The rounds' own gates, suites and ablations are in addenda `6216192076` and `6217048956`.

- `@objectstack/plugin-audit`: tests 53 files / 863 passed; `typecheck` exit 0 (test-typecheck ledger OK).
- `@objectstack/cli`: unit project 301 files / 4,496 passed; `typecheck` exit 0.
- CLI integration, run locally because the diff touches it:
  - the new door suite plus `data-commands.absent-database` and `schema-migrate.one-shot-family`: 147 / 147;
  - `json-stdout-purity.e2e` (nightly tier): 62 / 62.
- `@objectstack/dogfood` typecheck exit 0. Dogfood: the new pin plus the eight suites that read `sys_comment` or share the gate (the E6 pin among them): 9 files / 79 passed.
- **The bound case, before and after.** "Before" is ablation A0 below: main's whole-read thread probe put back.

  | reading | before | after |
  |:--|--:|--:|
  | real engine + `AuditPlugin` + SQLite (`comment-parent-pair.integration`, 2,607 rows): member served / total, of 2,303 visible | 1,766 / 1,766 | 2,303 / 2,303 |
  | same: administrator `total`, of 2,605 | 2,000 | 2,605 |
  | real `SecurityPlugin` + `AuditPlugin` stack at the HTTP door (dogfood, 4,151 comments, one thread each): member served, of 2,050 visible | 981 | 2,050 |

  The administrator's newest-20 read is served 20 rows, with a total past 2 × 2,000. An unreadable parent's comments stay hidden: another member's record, a vault object, a deleted record, and a thread naming no record. The thread-scoped read of one of them answers 0 rows and `total` 0.
- **No SYSTEM-composed read or leaf.** On the real stack, no SYSTEM read of `sys_comment` carries a leaf. The only SYSTEM reads are the two bounded probes: `thread_id` over `object_name $null`, and the D5 pair probe.

**Ablations.** Each negative pin was run red, then restored. Every mutation went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, and every restore was proven blob == HEAD with `git diff HEAD` empty. Unless noted, the pins are the two plugin-audit suites, run from `src`.

| leg | mutation | red |
|:--|:--|:--|
| A0 | main's whole-read thread probe put back | src 7 of 17. Dogfood through `dist`: marker present (`ablation-dist-preflight` exit 0), 4 of 5 red. Restore rebuilt and the marker proven absent |
| A1 | the stamped branch admits every stamped row | 11 |
| A2 | unstamped rows not probed | 5 |
| A3 | the unstamped probe's branch loses its `object_name IS NULL` conjunct | 2 |
| A4 | a leaf written without `canReadObject` | 1 |
| A5 | the consumer catches the read's refusal into deny-all | 2 (unit and real engine) |
| A6 | the stamp keeps a writer's own pair | 7 |
| A7 | the re-point not re-stamped | 2 |
| A8b | a D5.2 middleware-gated parent leafed (temporary mutation of `planParentReads`, not committed) | 9 |
| A9 | a delegated caller leafed (same file, not committed) | 2 |
| A10b | a refused page read not counted | 1 |
| A11 | a thread naming no record stamped | 7 |
| A12 | an update naming the pair without a thread not re-derived (patch round 1) | src 3. Dogfood through `dist`: marker present (`ablation-dist-preflight` exit 0), 2 red. Restore rebuilt and the marker proven absent |
| A13 | with no stored row, the writer's pair kept (patch round 1) | 1 |
| A14 | the multi-row pair-divergence refusal removed (patch round 2) | 2 (real engine and unit) |

Void legs, declared:
- The first A0 leg was a no-op: its replacement contained the anchor, the tool refused it, nothing landed, and its readings are discarded.
- A8 and A10 were refused the same way first (the replacement text already occurred), and were rerun as A8b and A10b.
- A4, A5 and A9 were rerun after a test-only restructure of the unit stand-in, with the same results.

**Gates.**
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derives 103 commands at `e499adaf6`: 23 paths, 2,276 changed lines, under the 3,000 threshold. All 103 exit 0. `--ran` reports 「103 derived, 103 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN」.
- `pnpm check:adr-symbol-anchors` exits 0. ADR-0139's anchors `comment-access-hooks.ts#READ_SCAN_LIMIT` and `#installCommentReadVisibility` still resolve.
- The first union had three real reds, all fixed:
  - the census prose figures;
  - `check:engine-double-contract` and `check:objectql-double-limit`, both on my unit stand-in. The stand-in was restructured; no ledger was touched.
- Three exit-3 prerequisites (missing `dist`, a shallow clone) re-ran green after a build and a fetch.

## Acceptance notes

- **No redaction and no query guard over the pair.** The pair is a parse of `thread_id`, which every reader of a row is already served and may already filter by, so it discloses nothing new. The pair gets no entry in `parent-field-query-guard.ts`; that guard covers value-bearing columns of the activity stream and the ledger, and `sys_comment` has no such column.
- **A wider read.** An unpinned comment read builds one branch per registered object: E5's activity cost, now on comments too. Every comment read also runs one SYSTEM probe over `object_name IS NULL`. After the backfill that probe finds nothing; until then it finds at most 2,000 rows.
- **Unparented threads.** A comment whose thread names no record keeps `null` / `null` forever, so the unstamped probe always scans it. It stays hidden, as before.
- **The comments checklist item.** The card asks for "the comments item's revision" to carry the same two notes, but no checklist item covers comment read inheritance: the comment-related items in `records-forms.json` are about feeds and posting. So only the attachments item was revised, and no item was invented.
- **Stale prose outside this card's surface.** `parent-record-read-gate.ts`'s `no-object-admission` warning still cites the activity stream's withheld-update re-read, and the comment gate now prints it too. The file is #22788's, so it is not touched here. Carrier: #22788.
